title: 皇冠岭恶搞前台简报
instruction:
您是负责支持 Crownridge Health Network 的 31 诊所前台的现场协调主管。周末，在 Hawthorne Supply 扩大了消息服务使用的 SPF 记录并让 DKIM 未签名后，预约提醒电子邮件遭到了欺骗，Ana Vanterpool 需要在周一早上 7 点之前可用的东西，因为协调员已经在接听病人的电话。从`incident_messages.docx`和`mailing_log.xlsx`开始工作，并在工作目录的顶层创建`crownridge_front_desk_briefing.docx`。该文件应该是为诊所现场协调员提供的前台简报，具有明确的目的和截止日期，然后是每个场景的行动表，让非技术协调员决定什么是足够真实的采取行动，对患者说什么，停止做什么，以及何时和如何升级。语言平静、平实，适合朗读；让每个动作变得明确，而不是依赖技术术语或模糊的指示。保留所提供的消息和日志中的区别，包括涉及可疑发件人、回复地址、链接或付款请求、已与消息交互的患者以及非预约提醒消息的情况。
包括一个简短的源处理注释，可以对所提供的日志的不一致日期、噪声率值和行级注释进行任何必要的处理，而不会将这些源缺陷转化为面向患者的声明。不要添加来源不支持的建议，不要告诉工作人员使用浏览器挂锁作为真实性证明，也不要要求患者透露凭据或付款详细信息。将简报保持在三页或更少，使用可读的表格文本，并将完成的文件写入工作目录顶层的`crownridge_front_desk_briefing.docx`。

---

上述文件位于`references/`中：

- `references/incident_messages.docx` — 包含 Ana Vanterpool、Antoni Hutchins、Marisol Mikkelsen、Magda Seaborne 和 Gitta Lombardi 的源电子邮件和采访式笔记，描述了欺骗事件、支持的真实性信号、面向患者的语言、升级处理和超出范围的通信。
- `references/mailing_log.xlsx` — 包含提供的用于验证每个场景操作表的场景记录。它包括发件人和回复观察、消息内容指示器、操作状态、日期、供应商费率字段以及限定或覆盖主列的行级注释。

将您完成的工作写入**当前工作目录的顶层**，使用以下文件名：
- `crownridge_front_desk_briefing.docx` — 一份精美的前台简报，其中包含每个场景的操作表和简明的源处理说明。 （完全使用此文件名将文件写入工作目录的顶层。；使用三页或更少。；使用适合非技术诊所现场协调员的简单语言。；操作表必须为每个提供的场景明确做出决定、患者措辞、禁止的操作和升级路径。；不要引入不受支持的技术或患者安全声明。）

除了这些文件名之外，不会收集任何内容。在其他地方或以任何其他名称编写的正确文件得分为零。

materials.description: 沿用南杨原题包实际文件与已有公开预览。
materials.note: DOCX 正文与表格单元格文字提取；不还原分页、字体与版式。
materials.text:
CROWNRIDGE HEALTH NETWORK
Weekend appointment-reminder incident notes
Compiled Sunday evening for Monday front-desk coordination
Ana Vanterpool | Messaging service owner
Over the weekend, appointment-reminder emails were spoofed. Hawthorne Supply widened the SPF record used by the messaging service, and DKIM was left unsigned. We are receiving patient calls across the 31 clinic front desks. Use the Crownridge messaging incident channel for suspicious-message reports; I am the owner contact for the incident.
Magda Seaborne | Security liaison
The visible sender address can be forged. It is not enough by itself to decide that a reminder is genuine. A browser padlock or an HTTPS appearance is not a test that the email itself is authentic. In the cases provided, a Crownridge reply-to can support other information, but it is not proof by itself.
Marisol Mikkelsen | Scheduling-system contact
For appointment questions, check Crownridge's internal scheduling record. The record is how staff should verify appointment information. Do not turn a caller into a technical verifier of the email.
Antoni Hutchins | Front-desk operations
Suggested call language: “We are aware of misleading appointment-reminder messages. I can check your appointment information in our scheduling record.” Do not ask callers to read credentials, payment-card information, or one-time codes. Do not direct a caller to a phone number, link, or reply destination supplied only by a suspicious message.
Ana Vanterpool | Messaging service owner
When a patient clicked or replied to a suspicious message, stop further interaction with that message. Do not request or repeat sensitive information. Record the report through the messaging incident channel and preserve the original message or a screenshot when available. Do not forward suspicious content to patients. This report does not establish that an account or identity was compromised.
Gitta Lombardi | Vendor liaison
A Hawthorne Supply communication about marketing operations or invoicing is not a patient appointment-reminder message. It is outside the front-desk patient-response workflow; do not treat every Hawthorne Supply communication as a patient spoof.
Working distinction: message authenticity signals and appointment verification are different questions. A plausible sender or reply-to never replaces checking the internal scheduling record.

gold.text:
Front-Desk Briefing: Appointment-Reminder Calls
Crownridge Health Network | For clinic site coordinators and front-desk staff | Use for calls before Monday, 7:00 a.m.
Purpose. Give patients a calm, consistent response after weekend spoofed appointment-reminder emails. Ana Vanterpool, messaging-service owner, is the incident contact. The visible sender address can be forged; a Crownridge reply-to is only a supporting signal. Neither proves a message is genuine. Check appointment information in Crownridge's internal scheduling record.
VERIFY
Use the internal scheduling record for appointment questions. Do not ask a patient to validate the email.
DO NOT USE AS PROOF
A browser padlock or HTTPS appearance is not proof that the email is authentic.
ESCALATE
Preserve the original message or screenshot when available. Send the report to Ana Vanterpool through the Crownridge messaging incident channel; do not forward suspicious content to patients.

Scenario actions
Incoming situation / trigger
Decision
Say to the patient
Stop doing
Escalate / next step
A. Routine reminder: Crownridge-looking sender and Crownridge reply-to; appointment details match the internal scheduling record; no payment or credential request.
Routine reminder after record check.
“I can confirm the appointment information in our scheduling record.”
Do not rely on the sender or reply-to alone; do not ask the patient to prove the email is real.
Answer appointment questions from the internal record. No incident escalation is needed for this corroborated case.
B. Unfamiliar link and non-Crownridge reply-to, even though the visible sender looks like Crownridge.
Suspicious. Do not act through the message.
“We are aware of misleading reminders. I can check your appointment in our scheduling record.”
Do not open or recommend the unfamiliar link, reply, or use a phone number supplied only in this message.
Keep the original or a screenshot when available; report through the Crownridge messaging incident channel to Ana Vanterpool.
C. Message appears from Crownridge but asks for payment, credentials, or a one-time code.
Suspicious.
“Please do not share payment or sign-in information from that message. I can check the appointment in our scheduling record.”
Do not request or repeat credentials, payment-card information, or one-time codes. Do not take payment through the message.
Preserve message/screenshot when available; report through the Crownridge messaging incident channel to Ana Vanterpool.
D. Patient already clicked a link or replied to a suspicious reminder.
Already interacted: use incident response.
“Please stop using that message. I can check your appointment in our scheduling record.”
Stop further clicking, replying, payment, or information exchange. Do not request or repeat credentials, payment-card information, or one-time codes.
Preserve message/screenshot when available; record the report through the Crownridge messaging incident channel to Ana Vanterpool. Do not state that an account or identity was compromised.
E. Hawthorne Supply marketing operations or invoice communication; not an appointment reminder.
Out of scope for patient workflow.
No patient wording: this is not a patient appointment-reminder call.
Do not convert this vendor item into a reminder response or tell patients it is a spoof.
Handle outside the front-desk patient workflow; it is not the same response for every Hawthorne Supply communication.
F. Crownridge reply-to, but appointment details are not sufficiently corroborated in the internal scheduling record.
Do not declare genuine; treat cautiously and escalate.
“I cannot confirm that message. I can check your appointment in our scheduling record.”
Do not treat the reply-to as proof. Do not direct the patient to the message link, reply destination, or any supplied phone number.
Preserve message/screenshot when available; report through the Crownridge messaging incident channel to Ana Vanterpool while using the internal record for appointment questions.
Source-handling note. This briefing applied row-level Notes as overrides to the log’s main columns. The date/time column mixes an ISO-style timestamp with a slash-separated date/time, so no exact chronology is inferred beyond the weekend-to-Monday context. The vendor-rate field includes insignificant floating-point decimal noise; it is source metadata, not a patient fee, threshold, or authenticity test.

original.grader_hint: Match each row to scenarios A-F from mailing_log.xlsx; merged rows count only if every scenario remains separately actionable.

criteria.description: 操作表为每个涵盖的场景提供了明确的决策或部署。
criteria.evidence: 决策/状态栏或同等散文。
criteria.grader_hint: 每个场景必须说明工作人员是否可以将其视为例行提醒、是否应将其视为可疑、是否应该升级或超出范围。

original.criterion: The action table gives a clear decision or disposition for every covered scenario.
original.grader_hint: Each scenario must say whether staff may treat it as a routine reminder, should treat it as suspicious, should escalate, or is out of scope.

criteria.description: 行动表为每个面向患者的场景提供了面向患者的措辞或具体句子。
criteria.evidence: 对患者说的列或等效的行文本。
criteria.grader_hint: 不要奖励行外的一般性建议；每个适用的行都需要可用的措辞。

original.criterion: The action table gives patient-facing wording or a concrete sentence to say for every patient-facing scenario.
original.evidence: Say-to-patient column or equivalent row text.
original.grader_hint: Do not award for generic advice outside the row; each applicable row needs usable wording.

criteria.description: 操作表为每个可疑或已经交互的场景提供了明确的停止指令。
criteria.evidence: 停止或不显示列或等效的行文本。
criteria.grader_hint: 查找与链接、回复、付款请求、凭据或提供的电话号码（如果适用）的禁止交互。

original.criterion: The action table gives an explicit stop-doing instruction for every suspicious or already-interacted scenario.
original.evidence: Stop or do-not column or equivalent row text.
original.grader_hint: Look for prohibited interaction with links, replies, payment requests, credentials, or supplied phone numbers as applicable.

criteria.description: 操作表给出了可疑和已经交互的场景的升级结果。
criteria.grader_hint: 该路线必须标识 Ana Vanterpool 或提供的 Crownridge 消息传递事件通道。

original.criterion: The action table gives an escalation outcome for suspicious and already-interacted scenarios.
original.grader_hint: The route must identify Ana Vanterpool or the supplied Crownridge messaging incident channel.

criteria.description: 简报指出，可见的发件人地址可以伪造。
criteria.grader_hint: 接受等效措辞（例如发件人显示或发件人地址）并不是证据。

original.criterion: The briefing states that a visible sender address can be forged.
original.grader_hint: Accept equivalent wording such as sender display or from-address is not proof.

criteria.description: 该简报并不将可见的发件人地址单独视为真实性证明。
criteria.grader_hint: 与 Crownridge 匹配的发件人仍必须得到证实或谨慎处理。

original.criterion: The briefing does not treat the visible sender address alone as proof of authenticity.
original.grader_hint: A sender matching Crownridge must still be corroborated or handled cautiously.

criteria.description: 例行证实的提醒不会仅仅因为其可见的发件人可能被伪造而被拒绝。
criteria.grader_hint: 该行应使用内部预约记录并提供支持信号，而不是一揽子拒绝。

original.criterion: The routine corroborated reminder is not rejected solely because its visible sender could be forged.
original.grader_hint: The row should use the internal appointment record and supplied supporting signals rather than a blanket rejection.

criteria.description: 该文件将 Crownridge 的回复视为支持信号，而不是独立的证据。
criteria.grader_hint: 检查回复是否在所有情况下都不会被忽略，也不会提升到足够的身份验证。

original.criterion: The document treats the Crownridge reply-to as a supporting signal rather than standalone proof.
original.grader_hint: Check that reply-to is neither ignored in all cases nor elevated to sufficient authentication.

criteria.description: 该文件并没有仅仅因为其回复属于 Crownridge 就宣布场景 F 真实。
criteria.grader_hint: 缺少预约证实必须导致谨慎或升级。

original.criterion: The document does not declare scenario F genuine solely because its reply-to belongs to Crownridge.
original.grader_hint: The missing appointment corroboration must lead to caution or escalation.

criteria.description: 简报指示工作人员使用 Crownridge 的内部日程安排记录来验证预约信息。
criteria.evidence: 可见的说明或耐心的措辞。
criteria.grader_hint: 提及内部调度系统的等效措辞是可以接受的。

original.criterion: The briefing directs staff to verify appointment information using Crownridge's internal scheduling record.
original.grader_hint: Equivalent wording referring to the internal scheduling system is acceptable.

criteria.description: 该简报并未指示患者使用仅由可疑消息提供的电话号码。
criteria.grader_hint: 检查患者的措辞和停止做的指示。

original.criterion: The briefing does not direct patients to use a phone number supplied only by a suspicious message.
original.grader_hint: Check both patient wording and stop-doing instructions.

original.criterion: The briefing does not direct patients to follow an unfamiliar link from the suspicious message.
original.evidence: Scenario B row and general guidance.

original.criterion: The briefing tells staff not to request or repeat credentials, payment-card information, or one-time codes.
original.grader_hint: All three sensitive-information categories should be covered or clearly encompassed.

criteria.description: 即使该消息看似来自 Crownridge，支付或凭证场景也会被归类为可疑。
criteria.grader_hint: 可疑分类不能仅取决于发件人字段。

original.criterion: The payment-or-credential scenario is classified as suspicious even if the message appears to come from Crownridge.
original.grader_hint: The suspicious classification must not depend only on the sender field.

criteria.evidence: 可见的警告或场景指导。
criteria.grader_hint: 接受简单语言的等效内容。

original.criterion: The briefing states that a browser padlock or HTTPS appearance is not proof that the email is authentic.
original.grader_hint: Accept plain-language equivalents.

criteria.grader_hint: 不要再进行点击、回复、付款或凭证交换。

original.grader_hint: Look for no further clicking, replying, payment, or credential exchange.

criteria.grader_hint: 必须指定 Ana Vanterpool 或 Crownridge 消息传递事件通道。

original.criterion: The already-clicked-or-replied scenario directs staff to use the supplied internal escalation route.
original.grader_hint: Ana Vanterpool or the Crownridge messaging incident channel must be named.

criteria.description: 已经交互的指南并未断言患者的帐户或身份已被泄露。
criteria.grader_hint: 该消息人士支持升级和谨慎，而不是确认的妥协。

original.criterion: The already-interacted guidance does not assert that the patient's account or identity was compromised.
original.grader_hint: The source supports escalation and caution, not a confirmed compromise.

criteria.grader_hint: 等效的证据保存措辞是可以接受的。

original.criterion: The briefing tells staff to preserve the original suspicious message or a screenshot when available.
original.grader_hint: Equivalent evidence-preservation wording is acceptable.

criteria.description: Hawthorne Supply 供应商或发票通信被识别为在患者预约提醒工作流程之外。
criteria.grader_hint: 它必须被排除在面向患者的行动之外，而不是转化为提醒响应。

original.criterion: The Hawthorne Supply vendor or invoice communication is identified as outside the patient appointment-reminder workflow.
original.grader_hint: It must be excluded from patient-facing action rather than converted into a reminder response.

original.grader_hint: A coordinator must be able to match the row to the incoming situation.

spec.professional_context: Crownridge Health Network is responding to a patient-facing email spoofing incident involving its appointment-reminder service and the Hawthorne Supply marketing vendor. Ana Vanterpool needs a concise briefing that clinic site coordinators can use consistently before the Monday morning operational deadline.
difficulty_sources: Translate technical email-authentication evidence into safe, unambiguous front-desk language
Preserve scenario-specific exceptions from messy source records
Distinguish supported actions from plausible but unsupported security advice
Handle mixed date representations and floating-point rate noise without creating false precision

source_set.semantic_relationship: The DOCX supplies the narrative and stakeholder guidance; the XLSX supplies the scenario-level observations. The gold briefing is a faithful restructuring of both sources, with row-level Notes taking precedence over conflicting main-column labels.

incident_messages_content.incident_summary: Ana Vanterpool's messaging service was spoofed over the weekend. Hawthorne Supply widened the SPF record used for the service and DKIM was left unsigned. The incident caused patient calls to 31 clinic front desks.
supported_authenticity_interpretation: The visible sender address can be forged and is not sufficient proof that an appointment reminder is genuine.
A reply-to address belonging to Crownridge is a useful supporting signal in the supplied cases, but it is not a reason to ask a patient to reveal information.
A browser padlock or HTTPS appearance is not an authentication test for the message and must not be presented as proof.
A message that asks for credentials, payment details, or an unfamiliar link is not to be acted on as an appointment reminder.
patient_language: Tell a caller that staff are aware of misleading appointment-reminder messages and will verify appointment information through Crownridge's internal scheduling record.
Do not ask the caller to read credentials, payment-card information, or one-time codes to the front desk.
Do not direct a caller to use a phone number, link, or reply destination supplied only by the suspicious message.
already_interacted_case: If a patient clicked or replied to a suspicious message, staff should stop further interaction with that message, avoid requesting or repeating sensitive information, record the incident through the supplied internal escalation route, and tell the patient that the clinic will use the verified scheduling record for appointment questions.
The briefing must not claim that a patient account was compromised unless the source states that fact.
scope_case: A Hawthorne Supply vendor communication about marketing operations or invoicing is not an appointment-reminder message and is outside the front-desk patient response workflow.
The briefing should identify that case as out of scope rather than converting it into a patient instruction.
incident_messages_content.escalation: The supplied notes identify Ana Vanterpool and the Crownridge messaging incident channel as the escalation route. The coordinator should preserve the original message or screenshot when available and avoid forwarding suspicious content to patients.

scenario_records.meaning: A routine appointment reminder whose visible sender resembles Crownridge, whose reply-to is the supplied Crownridge address, whose appointment details match the internal scheduling record, and which contains no payment or credential request.
scenario_records.notes_effect: No exception; use the main fields.

scenario_records.meaning: A message with a forged-looking Crownridge sender and a non-Crownridge reply-to that asks the recipient to use an unfamiliar link.
scenario_records.notes_effect: No exception; classify as suspicious and do not direct the patient to the link.

scenario_records.meaning: A message that appears to come from Crownridge but asks for payment or credentials.
scenario_records.notes_effect: The Notes field overrides the main action label and requires the message to be treated as suspicious.

scenario_records.meaning: A patient reports clicking or replying to a suspicious reminder.
scenario_records.notes_effect: The Notes field overrides the ordinary response field and requires the already-interacted escalation response.

scenario_records.meaning: A vendor-facing Hawthorne Supply operational or invoice communication that is not an appointment reminder.
scenario_records.notes_effect: The Notes field marks it out of scope for the front-desk patient workflow even if the main columns make it look actionable.

scenario_records.meaning: A message with a Crownridge reply-to but insufficient appointment corroboration in the internal scheduling record.
scenario_records.notes_effect: No exception; it must not be declared genuine solely from the reply-to address.

defects: The Notes column contains row-level exceptions that override the corresponding main action or classification columns; the exceptions occur in more than one scenario.
The vendor-rate field contains a floating-point representation with insignificant binary-style noise rather than an exact decimal equality.
The single date/time column mixes an unambiguous ISO-style timestamp with a slash-separated day/month value whose interpretation is ambiguous without the narrative context.
mailing_log_semantics.data_integrity: All substantive scenario facts are complete and mutually consistent after applying the row-level Notes overrides. There are no duplicate records, formula errors, missing required values, zero denominators, hidden images, or additional seeded defects.

gold_transformation.operation: Restructure the supplied narrative and scenario records into a concise DOCX briefing. Preserve supported facts, consolidate repeated guidance, and express each scenario as an explicit coordinator decision with patient wording, stop-doing instruction, and escalation outcome.
required_disclosures: State that the visible sender address can be forged.
State that a Crownridge reply-to is only a supporting signal and does not justify requesting sensitive information.
State that the browser padlock is not proof of message authenticity.
State that row-level Notes override the main columns.
Acknowledge the mixed date representation and explain the conservative treatment used for the briefing timeline.
Acknowledge the floating-point rate noise without presenting a falsely exact derived claim.
required_scenario_coverage: Patient who already clicked or replied
Insufficiently corroborated reminder with a Crownridge reply-to
gold_quality: A coordinator can choose an action on first reading without inferring missing steps.
Patient wording is calm and does not blame the patient.
The briefing does not tell staff to use the padlock, sender display, or reply-to alone as proof.
The briefing does not invent compromise, legal, clinical, or technical consequences not present in the sources.

original_instruction:
You are the site-coordination lead supporting Crownridge Health Network's 31 clinic front desks. Over the weekend, appointment-reminder emails were spoofed after Hawthorne Supply widened the SPF record used by the messaging service and left DKIM unsigned, and Ana Vanterpool needs something usable before Monday at 7am because coordinators are already taking patient calls. Work from `incident_messages.docx` and `mailing_log.xlsx` and create `crownridge_front_desk_briefing.docx` in the top level of the working directory. The file should be a front-desk briefing note for clinic site coordinators with a clear purpose and deadline, followed by a per-scenario action table that lets a non-technical coordinator decide what is genuine enough to act on, what to say to a patient, what to stop doing, and when and how to escalate. Keep the language calm, plain, and suitable for reading aloud; make each action explicit rather than relying on technical terms or vague instructions. Preserve the distinctions in the supplied messages and log, including cases involving a suspicious sender, a reply-to address, a link or payment request, a patient who has already interacted with a message, and a message that is not an appointment reminder. Include a short source-handling note that makes any necessary treatment of the supplied log's inconsistent dates, noisy rate value, and row-level notes visible without turning those source defects into patient-facing claims. Do not add advice that the sources do not support, do not tell staff to use a browser padlock as proof of authenticity, and do not ask patients to disclose credentials or payment details. Keep the briefing to three pages or fewer, use readable table text, and write the finished file as `crownridge_front_desk_briefing.docx` at the working-directory top level.

---

The files referred to above are in `references/`:

- `references/incident_messages.docx` — Contains the source emails and interview-style notes from Ana Vanterpool, Antoni Hutchins, Marisol Mikkelsen, Magda Seaborne, and Gitta Lombardi describing the spoofing incident, supported authenticity signals, patient-facing language, escalation handling, and out-of-scope communications.
- `references/mailing_log.xlsx` — Contains the supplied scenario records used to verify the per-scenario action table. It includes sender and reply-to observations, message content indicators, operational status, dates, a vendor rate field, and row-level notes that qualify or override the main columns.

Write your finished work to the **top level of the current working directory**, using exactly these filenames:

- `crownridge_front_desk_briefing.docx` — A polished front-desk briefing note with a per-scenario action table and a concise source-handling note. (Write the file into the top level of the working directory using exactly this filename.; Use three pages or fewer.; Use plain language appropriate for non-technical clinic site coordinators.; The action table must make the decision, patient wording, prohibited action, and escalation path explicit for every supplied scenario.; Do not introduce unsupported technical or patient-security claims.)

Nothing outside those filenames is collected. A correct file written anywhere else, or under any other name, scores zero.
